title: Hierarchical throttle and priority tiers for microbatch admission under extreme QPS
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: implement a hierarchical admission controller that enforces priority-aware microbatch thresholds and coordinated KV-cache eviction hints to maintain latency SLOs under sustained high QPS (spikes > 3x nominal). This ticket is focused on admission logic, signal fusion, and safe degradation paths rather than allocator internals or kernel changes.
background: We continue to see tail-latency regressions during multi-tenant spikes where concurrent small requests saturate GPU headroom and cause KV cache thrashing. Existing thresholding heuristics reduce throughput too aggressively for high-priority traffic or fail to reclaim KV memory quickly enough, leading to more RPC retries. This work complements ongoing work on continuous batching and KV eviction (runtime team). Related performance incidents: incident-2025-11-kv-hot-surge and benchmarks in /docs/benchmarks/q4-2025.
proposal: 1) Introduce a two-tier admission system: (A) fast fast-path local headroom check using running GPU slot estimate + reserved headroom for P0 traffic, (B) slow-path coordinator that rebalances microbatch budgets across slots every 500ms. 2) Add priority buckets (P0,P1,P2) with dynamic weight adjustments based on configured SLOs and recent error/latency signals. 3) Emit KV-eviction hints when predicted per-slot KV pressure exceeds threshold to downstream eviction controller to preemptively free key-space. 4) Implement additive smoothing (EWMA) over request arrival rate to avoid oscillation, with conservative ramp-down for recovered capacity. 5) Provide telemetry: per-bucket drop rate, admission latency, KV-eviction triggers, and headroom estimate uncertainty.
tradeoffs:
- Faster local checks reduce admission latency but can be conservative and underutilize GPU.
- Coordinator rebalancing improves fairness but adds control-plane complexity and possible synchronization jitter.
- Aggressive KV-eviction reduces memory pressure but may hurt cache hit rates; will require workload-specific heuristics.
- Introduces more knobs (bucket weights, smoothing windows) that will need sane defaults and automated tuning later.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (this ticket): implement admission controller and unit tests; expose config for bucket weights and smoothing windows. Phase 2: integrate KV-eviction hints and coordinator; run shadow experiments on canary fleet. Phase 3: rollout with canary -> 50% -> 100% with automatic fallback to previous admission policy if P99 latency regresses.
acceptance_criteria:
- New admission controller deployed in shadow mode for 48h with no actionable errors.
- Shadowed traffic telemetry shows no more than 2% increased tail latency for P0; total throughput reduction < 5% for same cost.
- KV-eviction hints trigger and downstream eviction reduces slot-level usage by >= 20% within 1s for synthetic hot-key test.
- Unit and integration tests cover edge-cases: zero-headroom, burst from 0->10k RPS, interleaved priority inversion.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: oscillation between admission and eviction. Mitigation: conservative smoothing and minimum hold times for eviction decisions.
- Risk: starvation of lower-priority traffic. Mitigation: implement soft-fairness token bucket and bleed-through caps.
- Risk: inaccurate headroom estimator on novel GPUs. Mitigation: feature-flag per-hardware calibration and fallbacks to conservative defaults.
test_plan:
- Synthetic high-QPS replay (3x and 5x nominal) with mixed priority distribution to validate admission behaviour.
- Hot-key KV stress test using /infra/load/hotkey-generator.
- End-to-end canary against real API routes with telemetry gating.
- Chaos: kill coordinator leader and ensure graceful fallback to local fast-path.
notes: Prototype implemented in branch feat/hierarchical-throttle. Initial microbenchmarks show 18% reduction in KV thrash events and stable P99 for high-priority traffic on 2080-series nodes. Need real-world canary on M60/RTX/next-gen to validate. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7234
updates: 2026-02-15: Spike complete. Implemented local headroom estimator using sliding-window slot availability and validated against emulator. Prototype lives in runtime admission module.
2026-02-22: Added priority buckets and EWMA smoothing. Observed underutilization at 1x load due to conservative defaults; adjusted weight schedule for P1 to allow minimal bleed-through.
2026-02-28: Integrated KV-eviction hint events (proto). Confirmed downstream eviction controller can consume hint and reclaim entries within 800ms in synthetic test.

2026-03-05: Benchmark run on canary pool (10% traffic) in shadow mode for 24h. Results: P0 p99 latency unchanged, P1 saw 3% throughput degradation, total token throughput -2%. Logging surfaced a jittery coordinator heartbeat under GC spikes — investigating.
2026-03-12: Fixed heartbeat jitter by switching coordinator state updates to atomic ring-buffer and backoff jitter. Preparing rollout plan for next cycle; drafting console dashboards for visibility.
reviews: PM review (Lena Ortiz) 2026-02-20: Approved prioritization; asked for explicit customer impact statement and rollout gates.
Design review (Samir Patel) 2026-02-24: UX for retired requests and rate-limit messaging approved; suggested adding per-route override controls in Console.
Security review (Maya Chen) 2026-03-03: No PII exposure; KV-eviction hints are metadata-only and acceptable.
Code review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7234 - requested added unit tests for zero-headroom path.
